correctness.rationale: For common atomless circular samples the rank interleavings produce exactly uniform weak compositions. At \(2\le n\le m\) the identity \(R=2nZ/m\) follows pointwise because positive occupancies are at least n/m. The Dirichlet-multinomial factorial moment identities and conditional-on-vacancy calculation give \(\operatorname{Var}(Z)\), \(\operatorname{Var}(Q)\), and \(\operatorname{Cov}(Z,Q)\) exactly; replacing R, factoring the denominator-minus-numerator, and the positive cubic in the balanced successive difference prove all claimed boundaries. The actual bundled standalone checker independently enumerated weak compositions for 2<=m,n<=7 and performed 9560 exact-rational assertions. Its finite checks do not substitute for the analytic all-parameter proof.

value.rationale: The result gives an exact, samplewise redundancy boundary for two established circular two-sample tests and an explicit, finite-sample dependence diagnostic for combining or comparing Rao and Dixon at precisely the balanced sample sizes studied in 2021 practice. The strictly changing linear residual from zero at two Y observations to \(1/2\) at large balance supplies a quantitatively meaningful test-dependence calibration beyond individual null distributions. It does not assert new hypothesis-testing power, independent information in a nonlinear sense, or a larger general theorem.
